content: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are considered the first-line therapeutic options for managing hypertension in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in those exhibiting significant levels of albuminuria. In individuals with severe albuminuria, defined as urinary albumin excretion of 300 mg/g or greater, the use of ACE inhibitors or ARBs has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). To maximize their therapeutic benefits, these medications should be administered at the highest doses that the patient can tolerate without adverse effects.
